answer: Before an agent's votes count, it locks a quartz bond released only after a public audit horizon. Auditors sample signed task histories and slash the stake when separate identities reuse the same distinctive claims. A Sybil attacker must fund every persona in advance and loses each detected bond, so multiplying identities raises capital at risk roughly linearly; honest agents recover their stake after passing audit. The ripple effect makes coordinated fake identities costly without requiring government IDs.
